metadata.title: A vertex maximum principle for subcritical reinforcement
metadata.description:
A self-contained alternative proof of unique strictly positive equilibrium and simultaneous almost-sure coordinatewise homogenization for subcritical graph-based reinforcement. The graph is countable, undirected and simple, with bounded degree; vertex firing rates are positive and bounded above, but their infimum may be zero. The exponent satisfies 0 <= alpha < 1. Initial edge counts are arbitrary finite deterministic positive integers. The proof uses finite-volume vertex minimization, an exact compensated jump transform, and a maximum principle for bounded positive complete vertex trajectories. Unrestricted nonnegative-equilibrium uniqueness is false; the positive statement is an explicitly corrected formulation.

Shuo Qin, arXiv:2610.11780v1, Theorem 1.1 (submitted 8 October 2026), supplies the full positive theorem and broader real initialization. It is prominently credited, together with the matching example in Remark 1.3, the older finite-WARM matching mechanism, and the 2018/2021 partial results of Couzinie and Hirsch. The vertex proof here is different, while the power/incidence and complete-limit strategy are shared structural ideas. Angel-Hermon-Yao work reported by Qin was not available as a verified full manuscript with a public date. Repository PR764 has a server creation date of 5 October 2026, but this does not certify the first public availability of current proof bytes. No first, sole, new-theorem or currently-open claim is made. The final publisher MATRIX chapter body was not obtained; question wording was checked against the official hosted pre-publication version.

The companion archive preserves all 63 frozen candidate files, distinct mathematical and priority reviews, bibliographic receipts, and reproducible integrity and finite diagnostic controls. Computation does not certify the infinite theorem or exhaustive priority. AI tools were used extensively in development, writing, reproduction, verification and adversarial review. This is an unrefereed preprint without external human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification. The note and companion materials are CC BY 4.0.
